title: fix(update): preserve FreeBSD pkg-owned files during self-update
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45233
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/147681

## What Problem This Solves

FreeBSD self-updates could replace files owned by `pkg`, including files reached through an installation alias or a global launcher. CLI and Gateway update admission did not verify native package ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

One bounded native `pkg` inventory inspector protects CLI/Gateway admission and package/Git mutation boundaries. It checks installation roots and launcher directory entries, including aliases, before activation, rollback, and cleanup. Owned or incompletely inspected paths produce an actionable refusal. The query cannot bootstrap `pkg`, invoke a configured query alias, or initialize a pkg plugin.

The inspection observes started asynchronous work and reports deadline failures. Launcher backup capture retains partial state so a later copy failure cleans earlier backups without moving the installation. Existing runtime preparation and Gateway admission remain behind their existing owners.

## User Impact

Package-managed installations update through their owning pkg or Ports deployment. Independently managed installations remain eligible when ownership is verified. Complete-inventory refusal is intentional: unreadable registered parents or exhausted inspection budgets cannot establish non-ownership. The observations do not atomically exclude a concurrent external pkg writer. Normal Linux, macOS, and Windows behavior is unchanged.

Published 2026.9.4 cannot acquire its FreeBSD update executor because process-start identity support is missing. A new target or `--no-restart` cannot repair that installed driver. The update guide now explains installation-owner recovery, preserving the existing prefix, configuration, state, and actual supervisor. pkg-owned installations must use pkg/Ports; npm must not overwrite them.

This does not complete rc.d/default-profile update support or certify a FreeBSD release. Both related issues remain open.

## Evidence

- Original CLI, Gateway, and activation failures were reproduced on unpatched source with an unowned control; the inspection-deadline unhandled rejection was also reproduced before repair.
- [Focused Crabbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34810814358): 336 tests across 13 files passed, with zero failures, skips, or unhandled errors. All 13 selected checks passed, including core graph/types, test types, scoped lint, and guards. Coverage includes partial launcher-backup cleanup, CLI/Gateway admission, aliases, deadlines, activation, and rollback. Full-source binding and runner cleanup passed. Independent source review found no actionable defect.
- [Native FreeBSD proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34817232757), x64 job 103893657871: all nine ownership cases passed, including unowned preview, owned custom/default roots, parent aliases, symlink-entry distinctions, unreadable-parent refusal, owned-launcher preservation after staging, and a subsequent changed-version activation using the same state.
- The same x64 job verified the published 2026.9.4 refusal without package replacement, then owner-assisted npm bootstrap and a candidate-owned update to `2026.9.99-first-hop.0`. Configuration and canonical state DB identity were retained. This is not a successful published-driver first hop or exhaustive user-data migration coverage.
- Native environment: FreeBSD 15.1, Node 24.21.0, pkg 2.8.4, fs-safe 0.10.0, and 60,442 pkg inventory entries. Producer build and artifact/source binding passed. All 28 product source blobs match the Crabbox-tested product commit `bb0ccc2facb02f5abba58a44d08bc2883ea42528`.
- Native artifact: ID `10336958654`, SHA-256 `4db0725505e8e1b831c53956ddd0d8cc9c2c19fd27d622cd443c07820ba399fd`, run attempt 1, source `dbe879170dc1262b4141b5dc3b5f6948a924ebff`. Candidate SHA-256 `a5b4e31615d37738e60a6b07fa006c59e38c99d7f521d3c0ca4c523370378cc8`; first-hop SHA-256 `acb3d9ab64905d61092e5df3d2deaed4508b8454e1424cfd6865c027051e0051`.
- **ARM64 follow-up:** job 103893657891 hit `ETIMEDOUT` in its initial npm install after 300 seconds, before any behavioral case. The log does not establish the cause. ARM installation/update availability remains unverified; diagnose that install with lifecycle output before rerunning. The changed guard adds no CPU/ABI-specific code, native artifact, or dependency change. Both x64 and ARM guests confirmed shutdown.
- The temporary workflow and fixture are removed. The recovery documentation link was verified with the current publishing parser, and the prior docs CI check passed. Production schema, configuration, and migration contracts are unchanged.
- The Git wrapper-retirement imports use existing OpenClaw filesystem owners; independent review passed. Historical native receipts retain their original source attribution.
- The prior final CI run on `7d32e52d10ab96ed91f57d6f7807ab16d96caeda` completed with 119 successful jobs and one failed QA test shard (plus the aggregate failure). Its [full-mode onboarding fixture timed out](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34838673131/job/103960102792); 1,154 sibling tests passed. Current main already contains [PR 147986](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147986), which removes unrelated repository docs scanning from that fixture without changing its assertions or timeout. The timeout's precise inner phase is not established.
- Current head `37ee89778af6929a232d9561baf7551ce78b4546` is rebased onto `78520903d4241cf66130abe43da215763caf9dc5`, including that QA correction and the already-landed Docker assertion repair. Every added/deleted production line is unchanged. The import conflict retains both main's snapshot imports and the FreeBSD filesystem imports. Four added test lines satisfy the new snapshot-source contract and assert that owned destinations are refused before snapshot work. Independent integration review, focused autoreview, and formatting passed.
- [Rebase integration proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34913031389) passed on the current head through Crabbox/Blacksmith Testbox: 321 tests across ten focused FreeBSD, snapshot, service-route, and dirty-checkout files; three Vitest shards completed successfully. All 48 pinned source-file hashes matched before and after execution. The one-shot lease `tbx_01m2h769en18nwrd963fta9697` confirmed stopped. Log SHA-256: `cfef75f6255304b0d10ab4cfd6557e41a11e144de487c89fa0ed75d7e9d39f70`. This is focused integration proof; the historical native proof retains its original source attribution.
- [Current required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34913086700) completed successfully on `37ee89778af6929a232d9561baf7551ce78b4546` (attempt 1); the required `openclaw/ci-gate` [job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34913086700/job/104210374052) is successful. No permanent qualification workflow or fixture is present in the final diff.
- Current-head ClawSweeper review completed at 2026-09-15 00:37 UTC with no actionable code or security findings. Its recorded complete-inventory refusal, concurrent external-writer limitation, and ARM proof gap are the documented accepted boundaries above. Its host could not retrieve raw logs; the maintainer directly inspected the test output, source bindings, and shutdown receipts. A successful Testbox workflow alone was not used as test proof.
